partners.mechanism_chain: COQ2 (HGNC:2563) —DISRUPTS→ Coenzyme Q biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-6798690); Coenzyme Q biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-6798690) —PRODUCES→ Coenzyme Q10 (Ubiquinone) (CHEBI:17795); Coenzyme Q10 (Ubiquinone) (CHEBI:17795) —BINDS→ Mitochondrial electron transport chain (GO:0005746); Mitochondrial electron transport chain (GO:0005746) —LEADS_TO→ Mitochondrial myopathy (HP:0003213); ATP5F1B (HGNC:33982) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial electron transport chain (GO:0005746); Mitochondrial electron transport chain (GO:0005746) —LEADS_TO→ Hypermetabolism (HP:0001947). Mutations in COQ2 (a gene involved in Coenzyme Q biosynthesis) lead to reduced Coenzyme Q10 levels, impairing the mitochondrial electron transport chain and causing mitochondrial myopathy (Disease A). Mutations in ATP5F1B, a subunit of ATP synthase, can lead to uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation, resulting in hypermetabolism and impaired ATP production (Disease B). Both diseases converge on the dysfunction of the mitochondrial electron transport chain.
